G01.title: The 152-ФЗ consent gate — one canonical record, three screens, and two bundles whose submit always fails
G01.why:
Three deployed bundles each carry their own consent screen, and they have drifted apart. `app.html` runs the canonical `AMayaConsent` and writes to `/client-channel/consent`; `app-tenant.html` and `maya-os-site/index.html` still run the older `AConsentGate` against the PHP relay; and `app.html` keeps a retired stub of that old gate — `function AConsentGate() { return null; }` (app.html:25143) — still mounted beside its replacement (app.html:39613) under a header comment that still describes the relay flow. The record itself is not duplicated: both routes end at one writer, `submitConsent` (client-channel-runtime.service.ts:187), reached directly (client-channel.controller.ts:121) and, via the bot's `/api/consent/submit` and the legacy bridge to the same service, indirectly (:259). The duplication is in the screens and the front doors, not in the store.

The two legacy screens cannot write at all. They submit `{accept_pdn: true, accept_marketing: …}` with no command identity, and a stable idempotency key is required twice over — at the relay (package5-client-consent-proxy.php:16, which answers `400 invalid_client_command`) and again by the canonical writer itself. Relaxing the relay check would not fix it; the field has to be sent, as `app.html` already sends it. Until then those clients are held by a gate they cannot pass, and see «Не удалось сохранить. Попробуйте ещё раз.» every time.

Each legacy copy also decides for itself who is exempt (`__meCurMode === 'staff'`, app-tenant.html:12208, maya-os-site:22047), how support forces the screen open (`?consent=1`), and what happens when the status call fails — a 401 there silently switches the gate off (app-tenant.html:12219-12232). And because both legacy bundles fetch their policy text from the salon's own relay, a white-label tenant's client is shown «ИП Мосин Станислав Евгеньевич, ИНН 263409096156» as the operator of their own data (webhook_server.py:4440, served at :4786). A consent record is a legal artifact; three screens, three exemption rules and someone else's operator name is the defect, not the UI.
G01.disappear:
The per-bundle copies: the two legacy `AConsentGate` screens, and in `app.html` the retired stub together with its mount and its stale header comment. The PHP relay hop for `consent_submit` (api-proxy.php → package5-client-consent-proxy.php) — but only after a working ingress is in `app-tenant.html` and `maya-os-site/index.html`; removing it first leaves those two bundles with no consent write at all. The retired Telegram accept callbacks, which today collapse `pdn_accept` / `mkt_accept` / `mkt_decline` into a single redirect to the app (bot.py:1751-1756). The passive booking-consent footnote in `app.html` legacy mode stops existing as a thing of its own — it has no checkbox, no receipt and no server call, and must never be counted as consent.

What does not disappear is the full-screen consent surface itself; only its three separate implementations do. And this entry does not settle which front door onto the one writer survives — the PWA's direct `/client-channel/consent` or the bot's `/api/consent/submit`, which the group's own proposed successor names. Both reach the same record; picking one is a decision still to be made, not a fact being reported.
G01.remain:
The consent record and its two independent decisions — personal data required, marketing optional. The canonical writer already stores them as two separate facts and already accepts a "no"; it is all three screens that can only ever transmit "yes" (`{privacy: true, …}`, app.html:25243; `accept_pdn: true` in both legacy copies), with nothing but a client-side tick in front of it. The successor must take the recorded decision from what was actually submitted, on the server.

The policy text remains a capability, with one correction to how it is carried across: what the legacy screens show is an excerpt, rendered only in the "sign the consent" state and never in the marketing-only one, and it names the salon as operator. Port the rendering, not the text — the successor needs the operator identity of the tenant whose client is reading it. (The full policy is shown before acceptance only in Telegram.)

The two states driven by server `status` — the full screen when personal-data consent is missing, the shorter «Рассылки» re-ask when only the marketing choice is outstanding. The behaviour that staff are not gated and that support can force the screen open, with the exemption decided on the server as `AMayaConsent` already does rather than by a client-side mode flag, and with the force-open unable to write a fresh record for a client who already has one. The booking-confirm slot keeps both of its branches: the legacy 152-ФЗ notice and the SaaS calendar-destination string that shares the slot.

And the gate keeps blocking — as a verified full-screen surface. Under the widget contract the consent kind may show the decision and hand off to that surface; it may not carry the accept control and collects nothing (§2.6.18 CONSENT.1, CONSENT.4, fullscreen required), and until the consent read capability is registered it cannot carry even the handoff (`GAP-CONSENT-READ`). Chat may bring the client to the gate; the signature stays on the surface. One property no copy has today must also be built in: when the status call fails, the gate fails closed.
G01.risk:
HIGH — and live now, not something the merge would introduce. Of the 126 rows in this dossier, every consent row sits in this one group (checked across all 26). Today: clients on the tenant and MayaOS bundles cannot record consent by any route, because every submit is rejected before it becomes a record; a Telegram client who cannot reach the app has no in-channel route either, since the consent buttons only redirect while the `group=-1` gate stops every non-exempt update (bot.py:4973); a refusal cannot be expressed anywhere, because acceptance is a constant in all three screens; and the gate switches itself off when its own status call fails — narrowly and recoverably in the legacy copies (401 only, retried every 800 ms), broadly and without recovery in the canonical one, where any 5xx on `/client-channel/status` hides the gate until the session token next rotates (app.html:25220, 25229). A tenant's client is additionally shown the wrong data operator.

The merge is the repair; the hazard is the status quo persisting — together with four ways to make it worse: copying the salon's policy text into a tenant's screen, keeping acceptance as a client-side constant, collapsing the two decisions into one "I agree", and inheriting the canonical component's silent self-disable as if it were the safe behaviour.

G01.objection: The correction still describes the merge target as the safe side, and it is not. Retiring the legacy `401 → done = true` branch is presented as closing a fail-open, but `AMayaConsent` fails open wider and does not recover: it sets `checkedSession` before the status fetch (app.html:25220) and never resets it in the `.catch`, which calls `setShow(false)` (25229), while `meWidgetAf`'s `finalize` throws on any non-2xx — so one 500/503 or network blip on `/client-channel/status` hides the legal gate until the session token rotates, with the 800 ms re-check short-circuiting the whole time. The legacy gate fails open only on an explicit 401 and resets `checkedRef.current` on 5xx, retrying. As written, the merge trades a narrow recoverable fail-open for a broad persistent one, and "fail closed on a status error" has to be a build requirement of the successor, not an assumed inheritance. Second, in the same direction: "port the `privacy_text` accordion INTO the successor" would carry «ИП Мосин Станислав Евгеньевич, ИНН 263409096156» to a white-label tenant's client as their data operator — the rendering is the capability, the salon's text is a defect. Both are cases of a hazard described as an improvement, which is the error class an owner cannot catch from the page.

G02.why: Six inventory rows describe one thing a user would name once: the same ATeamChat component in three HTML builds (`app.html` S-040, `app-tenant.html` S-142, `maya-os-site/index.html` S-100), plus two parts of the `app.html` one — the `?team=main` deep-link mount (S-064) and its voice recorder (S-282) — and the NestJS controller the `app.html` copy posts to (S-272, a `team-communications.controller.ts` file carried in the inventory as channel `pwa`, kind `notification`). The deep-link overlay is not a convenience added because the tab was hard to reach: its own anchor (L33983) sits in AStaffDashboard, which the router never renders — `window.ALivePanel` is always assigned (L37629) and wins the `panel` fallback (L39152) — so in `app.html` the team surface is reached only by a hand-typed `?team=main` URL, which S-272 describes as a surface nobody finds by design. In a chat-first rebuild where primary navigation collapses from 112 reachable surfaces to five destinations, this belongs in one authority-scoped lane of the single conversation surface — with MAYA present rather than adjacent — not in a second, hidden chat application.

One primary-navigation entry goes with them — the team tab in `app-tenant.html` (S-142, `STAFF_TABS` index 3, L21844); the other five rows are sub-states beneath primary navigation rather than entries in it. The controller's `@Roles` list (TENANT_OWNER, BUSINESS_OWNER, TENANT_ADMIN, ADMINISTRATOR, STAFF) must be carried into the lane selector and stay enforced where it is enforced today, on the server; S-272 states it is the only thing keeping staff traffic out of client threads.
G02.risk: MEDIUM-HIGH — above the MEDIUM the group line carried, below G01's statutory HIGH, because three hazards outrank the upload path the old line named. First, the 152-ФЗ boundary: merging human-to-human and human-to-AI chat into one shell without unmistakable provenance lets a master post a client's personal data into a thread they believe is internal (S-142), and the standing rule is that client PD never reaches the LLM. Second, the recorder: it tears its streams down on unmount (S-282 L38314), so a lane that mounts and unmounts with messages risks leaving a live microphone open; its iOS-first MIME order ['audio/mp4','audio/webm;codecs=opus','audio/ogg;codecs=opus'] (L38311) breaks recording on Safari/WKWebView if reordered; and it is not the composer mic — it stores an attachment rather than producing a transcript, so "merge the two voice paths" would replace a persisted staff voice message with text and lose the audio. Third, authority: `@Roles` on the controller is the only barrier between staff traffic and client chats (S-272), so the lane selector must enforce it on the server rather than by hiding the lane. Transport ranks below these but is real — per-chunk receipt verification and resumability must survive the merge, and a feed that polls every 10 seconds folded into a push/realtime chat changes delivery latency (S-272). And for the `maya-os-site` copy on the legacy МЭ proxy this is a rebuild, not a re-parent (S-100), with parity to be proven against a surface most people have never seen (S-282).

G03.title: The staff client base — the same list twice
G03.why: A legacy tab in `app.html` and the `AStaffClients` screen in `maya-os-site` are two implementations of one server projection: both read the same legacy proxy action `panel_master_clients` (L28522 / L25698) and both return a client list with revenue totals scoped to the logged-in master. Both already carry the `notmaster` state that explains an empty list to a non-master account (L28526 / L25702) — it is not a feature one of these two contributes to the other. The surface with no equivalent message is the SaaS clients tab they would fold into: the tenant-API-backed, manager-scoped `panel#clients` (L31305), which the evidence points at but which no signed record yet names as the target. Each copy survives only as a fall-through, and for different reasons: in `maya-os-site` managers are already routed to `panel#clients` (L23477), leaving `AStaffClients` as the implementation for non-managers; in `app.html` the staff bar prefers the SaaS cabinet and reaches the legacy tab only when the SaaS context is absent (L26474-26479). Collapsing them is ONE MAYA — DIFFERENT AUTHORITY: one `clients` capability whose scope — own clients or all — is decided by authority on the server, not by which of two screens an account happens to land on.

The `notmaster` refusal remains — but it has to be built into whichever surface absorbs these two, not inherited from it: the SaaS clients tab carries no equivalent message today. The staff bar indicator also has to be re-keyed, since the legacy tab's nav index is recorded as the only thing keeping that indicator honest on that screen.

The target, `panel#clients`, is tenant-API backed and manager-scoped: merging into it without adding self-scoping would either expose the whole client base to a plain master or remove their client list entirely. Scope here is server-side authority over who may see whose client records, and since the fundamental rules hold fail-closed in only 13 of 21 cases, that self-scoping has to be demonstrated under the K16 parity condition rather than assumed to fail safe. Both copies also still run on the legacy `panel_master_clients` proxy while the target is tenant-API backed, so this is a re-implementation of the projection, not a re-parenting of it. It is not higher than MEDIUM because nothing is removed before parity: both rows retire only after parity (K16) and the successor is still unnamed pending signature, so the parity gate itself would have to fail before the exposure could reach a master's screen.

G04.title: The work cabinet tab strip — two copies of it, and two of its nine tabs
G04.why: The same work cabinet exists in both bundles — `S-024` in `app.html`, `S-091` in `maya-os-site/index.html` — and its nine tabs (`appts|biz|mystat|customers|team|calendar|services|schedule|profile`) overlap almost completely with ASaasOwnerPanel's nine: two implementations of one work cabinet, reached by two different taps of the same bar. It is one of the largest families in the inventory — the two strip rows in this group sit on top of nine further rows carrying the app.html copy's own tabs, eleven of the 101 Maya-owned primary-nav entries the rebuild is meant to collapse, and that is before the cabinet's other shell row and its duplicate Сессии row are counted. The strip is a container and not a capability — the tabs lazy-load on tap and `services` renders exactly one card — but the strip's own code is load-bearing: the fine-grained predicates `saasIsCalManager()` / `saasCalInternal()` / `meAppAccessViewManager()` run where the tab list is built (L13975-13982), and the tap handler beneath it (L13984) is the only place the journal's data is fetched. The strip also manufactures the ambiguity chat-first removes: `calendar` and `schedule` both render the literal label «Расписание» and both appear at once for an internal-calendar manager.
G04.disappear: Both copies of the strip, the tab bar, and the hosting of a business cabinet inside the client `book` screen. All four rows are RETIRE AFTER PARITY — K16, so nothing here is removed at the moment of the merge, only after its target is proven reachable. One thing does not simply fall away with the strip: the tab-keyed bottom-bar mapping (`NAV_BY_SAAS_CAB_TAB = { mystat: 2, profile: 3 }`, L36204). The strip that feeds it goes, but S-091 records that mapping as something the merge must keep resolving, and the two tabs it keys are dispositioned on rows outside this group — so re-keying it is work the merge owes, not a saving it delivers.
G04.remain: The capability behind each tab — but this group names destinations for only three of the nine: `calendar`, `services catalog`, `schedule`. The other six (`appts`, `biz`, `mystat`, `customers`, `team`, `profile`) are dispositioned on their own rows and not here, and they do not all end the same way: `biz` is kept as a fullscreen detail reached by handoff rather than retired, and `profile`/Сессии is retired as UI with the fence kept server-side. This group is therefore not a nine-for-nine parity promise. The tab names must stay resolvable: `?cabinet=<tab>` deep links (allowlist L35674) and the bottom bar both address tabs by name, and that vocabulary survives as intent vocabulary rather than disappearing with the strip. Two capabilities live only in the cabinet copy and are lost by a naive merge into the owner panel: the device/session list with revoke and logout, which has no counterpart in ASaasOwnerPanel's `profile` tab, and `mystat`, the only self-scoped statistics view a plain staff member has. The successors must also carry the visibility rules the tabs carried — the journal under `saasIsCalManager()`, Услуги and Расписание under `saasCalInternal() && saasIsCalManager()` — and `svcCard`'s inline row-editor state `myCalSvcEdit`.
G04.risk: MEDIUM-HIGH — the failure modes here are silent rather than loud. `calendar` is the sole trigger for both `loadMyStaff()` and `loadMyJournal()` (L13984) and the render body re-checks only `myTab` (L14172), so a naive merge leaves the journal unhydrated and without its only client-side gate; `svcCard` is the only consumer of `myCalSvcEdit` (L14351), so a re-parent that drops that state turns per-service editing read-only with no error, and a reordered hydration leaves `svcCard` rendering against a null `myCal`; and because the bottom bar and `?cabinet=` links resolve tabs by name — the post-onboarding redirects emit `onboarded=1&…&cabinet=<tab>` and `cabinet=schedule&calendar_setup=1` (app.html L7196, L7205) — an un-rekeyed merge strands both deep links and the return path out of onboarding. G12.why: Eight of these nine already live inside the conversation, so for them the question is not whether they stay in chat but which contract kind each becomes — a real decision, because today they are hand-built components and hard-coded chip arrays with their own dispatch code. The profile card is the one that splits: its identity readout belongs in the chat's own identity affordance, its navigation rows belong in settings. The ninth, the owner expense confirmation card, is explicitly **not** a chat widget: it is a persistent owner surface, and it belongs in this group only because it is a third approval vocabulary doing the same job as `saasAiApprovalCard` and the chat widgets. The action-button dispatcher is the hard case: its vocabulary is strictly *larger* than the widget contract — `run_job` (which sends `__runjob:<job>` to the legacy chat endpoint), bare `screen` targets, arbitrary http/tel/mailto URLs, and synonym sets that are still live traffic from older server producers and from persisted history — so moving to declared intents is a capability cut, not a translation, and each item needs its own named disposition. `repeat_booking` is simultaneously an action and a widget trigger (it injects the book widget with prefill), so it migrates first and carefully.
G12.disappear: The hand-built components and their dispatch code; the five hard-coded quick-reply arrays and the separate welcome-screen chip renderer; the client-side synthesis of proactive messages, which today bypasses `notify_prefs` and quiet hours entirely. What does *not* simply disappear is the part of the action vocabulary with no widget equivalent — `run_job` with its legacy-endpoint call and its rich owner card, the bare `screen` targets, the URL escape hatch, and the synonym sets (`open_subs` / `open_subscriptions` / `subscription(s)` / `shop_subs`). None of these can be translated into a declared intent, so each needs a named disposition before the merge — carried across as an intent of its own, re-homed, or dropped deliberately — and dropping one is a decision to be signed, not a side effect of the merge. Pruning the synonyms in particular silently drops cards emitted by older server code paths and by history already persisted, so that is a change with consequences rather than a rename.
G12.remain: Every card a user sees today, with one documented exception: SaaS tenants already get a hard-coded empty history list (L16334), so for those clients there is no history content to preserve and the merged timeline must emit an explicit "unavailable" signal rather than inherit that silence. The per-visit paid amount that only the history rows carry (`[service, date, sum]`), and the active-subscription remaining visits that only the shop card shows. The loyalty suppression rule (balance ≤ 0 or no items) together with a replacement for its only frequency cap, and the repeat-booking inference with its self-suppression when an upcoming appointment already exists. The role-keyed quick replies as declared intents — and, for the client set, their exact label text, which `chatWidgetIntent` matches on, so a relabel silently stops producing the card; the staff and owner chips are questions put to MAYA instead, a second behaviour the one contract still has to represent. And the profile card's identity readout: it is not an authority check — enforcement stays server-side — but it is the client's only view of which identity MAYA is acting as, so removing it weakens the user's own verification, and a merged identity component must read both the legacy and the SaaS source or the legacy tenant shows a blank name.

Tenant isolation: the shop card self-hides on foreign tenants (`__ME_FOREIGN_TENANT` / `meIsMeTenant`, L16268), and a merged component that renders from `APP_DATA` without that guard is a cross-tenant content leak — one salon's subscription and certificate catalogue rendering inside another tenant's chat; separately, the history widget is hidden outside legacy by the dispatcher (L16188), a gate a merged widget key does not inherit automatically. Availability: the client surface re-shows default chips after every MAYA answer (L21669) and the welcome chips are the only affordance on an empty chat, so a server-driven list must return chips on every turn or a network hiccup leaves a chat-first product blank below the composer. Every one of these is a hazard the merge would create, not a defect running today — the one exception is the client-synthesised proactive cards, which already bypass `notify_prefs` and quiet hours.
